verdict.rationale: Gecko does provide API keys with owner attribution and usage logging (gecko-security-docs-11) and a rotate-token endpoint (gecko-security-docs-12), and its AI-tool integration lets an agent pull data via the API (gecko-security-docs-9/10), but there's no documented scoped/least-privilege permission model (e.g., read-only vs. write scopes) for these credentials. Community reports directly contradict a least-privilege design: the OAuth flow requests broad 'act on my behalf' / write-profile permissions rather than fine-grained repo access, which users explicitly flagged as concerning and non-scoped (gecko-security-comm-1, gecko-security-comm-7). missing for 10: explicit scoped/least-privilege API key creation UI, documented permission tiers, and resolution of the OAuth over-broad-scope complaint.
